Applying a [composited value](WEB-ANIMATIONS-1#composited-value) to a [target property](WEB-ANIMATIONS-1#target-property) is achieved by adding a specified value to the CSS cascade.

The level of the cascade to which this specified value is added depends on the [class](WEB-ANIMATIONS-1#animation-class) of the [animation](WEB-ANIMATIONS-1#concept-animation) [associated with](WEB-ANIMATIONS-1#animation-effect-associated-animation) the effect with the highest composite order in the [effect stack](WEB-ANIMATIONS-1#effect-stack) for a given property. By default, the specified value is added to the [Animation Origin](CSS-CASCADE-5#cascade-origin-animation) of the cascade. \[CSS-CASCADE-3\]

Tests

*   [applying-the-composited-result.html](https://wpt.fyi/results/web-animations/animation-model/combining-effects/applying-the-composited-result.html) [(live test)](http://wpt.live/web-animations/animation-model/combining-effects/applying-the-composited-result.html) [(source)](https://github.com/web-platform-tests/wpt/blob/master/web-animations/animation-model/combining-effects/applying-the-composited-result.html)

> **Example:** For example, if the effect with the highest composite order is associated with a “CSS transition”-class animation, the [composited value](WEB-ANIMATIONS-1#composited-value) will be added to the [Transition Origin](CSS-CASCADE-5#cascade-origin-transition) of the cascade.

The [composited value](WEB-ANIMATIONS-1#composited-value) calculated for a CSS [target property](WEB-ANIMATIONS-1#target-property) is applied using the following process:

1.  Calculate the *base value* of the property as the value generated for that property by finding the [computed value](CSS-CASCADE-5#computed-value) for that property in the absence of animations.

2.  Establish the [effect stack](WEB-ANIMATIONS-1#effect-stack) for the property (see [§ 5.4.2 The effect stack](WEB-ANIMATIONS-1#the-effect-stack)).

3.  Calculate the [composited value](WEB-ANIMATIONS-1#composited-value) of the [effect stack](WEB-ANIMATIONS-1#effect-stack) passing in the *base value* of the property as the initial [underlying value](WEB-ANIMATIONS-1#underlying-value) (see [§ 5.4.3 Calculating the result of an effect stack](WEB-ANIMATIONS-1#calculating-the-result-of-an-effect-stack)).

4.  Insert the [composited value](WEB-ANIMATIONS-1#composited-value) into the CSS cascade at the level defined for the [class](WEB-ANIMATIONS-1#animation-class) of the [animation](WEB-ANIMATIONS-1#concept-animation) [associated with](WEB-ANIMATIONS-1#animation-effect-associated-animation) the effect at the top of the [effect stack](WEB-ANIMATIONS-1#effect-stack) established for the [target property](WEB-ANIMATIONS-1#target-property).

An **effect stack** is associated with each property [targeted](WEB-ANIMATIONS-1#target-property) by one or more [keyframe effects](WEB-ANIMATIONS-1#keyframe-effect). The [effect stack](WEB-ANIMATIONS-1#effect-stack) establishes the relative composite order of keyframe effects.

The relative **composite order** of any two [keyframe effects](WEB-ANIMATIONS-1#keyframe-effect) *A* and *B* within an [effect stack](WEB-ANIMATIONS-1#effect-stack) is established by comparing their properties as follows:

1.  Sort *A* and *B* by applying the following conditions in turn until the order is resolved,

    1.  If *A* and *B*’s [associated animations](WEB-ANIMATIONS-1#animation-effect-associated-animation) differ by [class](WEB-ANIMATIONS-1#animation-class), sort by any inter-class composite order as defined for the corresponding classes.

    2.  If *A* and *B* are still not sorted, sort by any [class](WEB-ANIMATIONS-1#animation-class)-specific composite order defined by the common class of *A* and *B*’s [associated animations](WEB-ANIMATIONS-1#animation-effect-associated-animation).

    3.  If *A* and *B* are still not sorted, sort by the position of their [associated animations](WEB-ANIMATIONS-1#animation-effect-associated-animation) in the [global animation list](WEB-ANIMATIONS-1#global-animation-list).

[Animation effects](WEB-ANIMATIONS-1#animation-effect) that sort earlier have *lower* composite order.

The [effect value](WEB-ANIMATIONS-1#effect-value) of a single property referenced by a [keyframe effect](WEB-ANIMATIONS-1#keyframe-effect) as one of its [target properties](WEB-ANIMATIONS-1#target-property), for a given *iteration progress*, *iteration index* and *underlying value* is calculated as follows.

1.  If *iteration progress* is [unresolved](WEB-ANIMATIONS-1#unresolved) abort this procedure.

*This section is non-normative*At a given moment, an [animation effect](WEB-ANIMATIONS-1#animation-effect) can be in one of three possible *phases*. If an animation effect has an [unresolved](WEB-ANIMATIONS-1#unresolved) [local time](WEB-ANIMATIONS-1#local-time) it will not be in any phase.

The different phases are illustrated below.

![An example of the different phases and states
used to describe an animation effect.](images/animation-effect-phases-and-states.svg)

An example of the different phases and states used to describe an [animation effect](WEB-ANIMATIONS-1#animation-effect). 

The phases are as follows:

[before phase](WEB-ANIMATIONS-1#animation-effect-before-phase) 

The [animation effect](WEB-ANIMATIONS-1#animation-effect)’s [local time](WEB-ANIMATIONS-1#local-time) falls before the effect’s [active interval](WEB-ANIMATIONS-1#active-interval) and [end time](WEB-ANIMATIONS-1#animation-effect-end-time), *or* occurs during the range when a negative [start delay](WEB-ANIMATIONS-1#start-delay) is in effect.

[active phase](WEB-ANIMATIONS-1#animation-effect-active-phase) 

The [animation effect](WEB-ANIMATIONS-1#animation-effect)’s [local time](WEB-ANIMATIONS-1#local-time) falls inside the effect’s [active interval](WEB-ANIMATIONS-1#active-interval) and outside the range of any negative [start delay](WEB-ANIMATIONS-1#start-delay) or negative [end delay](WEB-ANIMATIONS-1#end-delay).

[after phase](WEB-ANIMATIONS-1#animation-effect-after-phase) 

The [animation effect](WEB-ANIMATIONS-1#animation-effect)’s [local time](WEB-ANIMATIONS-1#local-time) falls after the effect’s [active interval](WEB-ANIMATIONS-1#active-interval) or after the [end time](WEB-ANIMATIONS-1#animation-effect-end-time) if that comes first (due to a negative [end delay](WEB-ANIMATIONS-1#end-delay)), but *not* during the range when a negative [start delay](WEB-ANIMATIONS-1#start-delay) is in effect.

In addition to these phases, an [animation effect](WEB-ANIMATIONS-1#animation-effect) can also be described as being in one of several overlapping *states*. These states are only established for the duration of a single [animation frame](WEB-ANIMATIONS-1#animation-frame) and are primarily a convenience for describing stative parts of the model.

These states and their usage within the model are summarized as follows:

[in play](WEB-ANIMATIONS-1#in-play) 

Corresponds to an [animation effect](WEB-ANIMATIONS-1#animation-effect) whose [active time](WEB-ANIMATIONS-1#active-time) is changing on each frame.

[current](WEB-ANIMATIONS-1#current) 

Corresponds to an [animation effect](WEB-ANIMATIONS-1#animation-effect) that is either [in play](WEB-ANIMATIONS-1#in-play) or could become in play in the future based on its [animation](WEB-ANIMATIONS-1#concept-animation)’s current [playback rate](WEB-ANIMATIONS-1#playback-rate).

[in effect](WEB-ANIMATIONS-1#in-effect) 

Corresponds to an [animation effect](WEB-ANIMATIONS-1#animation-effect) that has a resolved [active time](WEB-ANIMATIONS-1#active-time). This occurs when either the animation effect is in its [active phase](WEB-ANIMATIONS-1#animation-effect-active-phase) or outside the active phase but at a time where the effect’s [fill mode](WEB-ANIMATIONS-1#fill-mode) (see [§ 4.6.8 Fill behavior and fill modes](WEB-ANIMATIONS-1#fill-behavior)) causes its active time to be resolved. Only [in effect](WEB-ANIMATIONS-1#in-effect) animation effects apply a result to their target.

The normative definition of each of these states follows.
